description: Energy Disruption Maps is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by U.S. Energy Information Administration; DOE, U.S. Department of Energy; NOAA | National Hurricane Center. View real-time maps of current and forecasted hazards overlain on the locations of energy infrastructure. Users can monitor potential threats to electricity supply in real-time from hazards such as tropical storms and hurricanes, flooding, and wildfires. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds, Wildfire. Assets: Critical Facilities, Energy and Utilities, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Transportation and Mobility. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
